rationale:
The reviewed tests cover each obligation of `requirements.sdk.outlines.selection`. All are in `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs`. I did not request implementation source, because the supplied tests were enough to judge adequacy.

- **Resolution from the root, returning an owned item.**
  - `rust_items_attach_documentation_and_preserve_structural_hashes` selects every outline item by its selector. It asserts `text()` equals the item's source span and `structural_hash()` equals the item's hash. It also selects `""` and a nested `mod[auth]/fn[check]`.
  - `markdown_heading_levels_resolve_encoded_duplicates_and_anonymous_items` selects percent-encoded names, `#N` duplicates and `block@hash` anonymous items. It also calls `select` on an already-selected item (`second.select(main)`) and gets the root-relative result.
  - `unicode_spans_use_bytes_and_whitespace_only_lines_create_no_items` selects `line` items and checks the text.
- **Shares the snapshot and the outline, with no extra read.**
  - `std::ptr::eq(function.outline(), contents.outline())` and the same assertion on `second` show the outline is shared.
  - `selected_contents_outlive_handles_and_later_file_edits` drops the original handle and overwrites the file on disk. Afterwards `selected` and `selected_again` keep their text and fingerprint, and `selected.select("")` still returns the original `"first\nsecond\n"`. That proves no re-read and no dependence on the dropped handle. `from_id` fails after the edit, which contrasts with `select`.
- **Shared fingerprinting rules.** `explicit_languages_share_configuration_and_retain_their_scheme` selects `part[selected]` from the supplied and path-loaded roots. The two fingerprints are equal. A language with a different scheme gives a different fingerprint.
- **`id()` and `text()` before redaction.** The `id()` assertions are in `selected_contents_outlive_handles_and_later_file_edits`, for both a selected item and the retained root. `formatted_contents_redact_credentials_while_retaining_raw_text_and_spans` shows the selected `text()` keeps the credential while `format()` redacts it. Rust selection includes attached docs and attributes (`starts_with("/// Check tokens.")` and `contains("#[inline]")`).
- **Identical plain-text lines are interchangeable.** `ambiguous_items_are_errors_except_for_identical_plain_text_lines` and `unknown_extensions_keep_nonblank_lines_and_content_selectors` check this. The first selects the shared selector of two identical `same` lines and gets `"same"`. The second selects the repeated `alpha` selector and gets `"alpha"`.
- **Errors for invalid, missing and ambiguous selections.**
  - `missing_file_and_invalid_selections_are_errors` covers the malformed selector `fn[` and the missing item `fn[absent]`.
  - `ambiguous_items_are_errors_except_for_identical_plain_text_lines` covers ambiguity. Duplicate `part[same]` items with the same hash must error. Duplicate `line[same]` items with different hashes must also error, so the line exemption applies only to identical content. The test asserts the message contains "ambiguous".
  - `css_duplicate_names_are_numbered_after_normalization_within_each_parent` covers the unnumbered `rule[a%20b]` selector. It errors because several siblings share the name.
- **Selector-syntax behavior used by selection.** The empty selector selects the root, and percent-encoding and `#N` numbering are exercised through `select`. The CSS, Markdown and Rust tests do this in several languages.

I found no obligation that lacks a test with a relevant assertion. The only unexercised input is a nonexistent `line@hash` selector. It falls in the already-tested "missing item" class, so I don't count it as a gap. All the tests carry `{test}` references to the subject.

text: :::{req} selection
`OutlineContent::select` resolves a selector from the file's root against the
retained outline. It returns another owned `OutlineContent` for that item,
sharing the original source snapshot and fingerprinting rules. Selection
performs no additional file read and remains usable after the original handle
is dropped. Resolution follows
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.selector_syntax`, including its rule that
identical plain-text lines are interchangeable. Invalid, missing, or ambiguous
selections return an error under {cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.errors`.
```rust,ignore
impl OutlineContent {
/// Select an item from this retained file snapshot.
pub fn select(&self, selector: &str) -> Result<Self, OutlineError>;
/// Address of the selected item.
pub fn id(&self) -> &OutlineId;
/// Original selected text, including attached source, before redaction.
pub fn text(&self) -> &str;
:::{req} selector_syntax
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
hash under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Siblings whose
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
:::{req} errors
The outline API makes a best effort to recover from parse errors.
File-read and unrecoverable parsing failures return errors, distinct from
successful contents for an empty file. Selecting a language commits to that
language's parsing rules.
A malformed selector, a missing item, or an ambiguity not permitted by
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.selector_syntax` also returns an error.
